def:finite-interface.title: Finite classical Einstein--Standard-Model interface
def:finite-interface.note: Encoded (FiniteInterfaceRepresentationTable.lean extends the (I1)-(I5) record FiniteInterface of FiniteEinsteinStandardModelInterface.lean). TabulatedFiniteInterface h adds the declared branch (minimal | neutrino), a linear equivalence tableEquiv : OneGeneration ~= C^{TableRow b} that INTERTWINES fermionRep with tableRep b, the block-diagonal sum of the table rows repQL, repLL (left) and repUR, repDR, repER (right), plus repNR on the neutrino branch, all taken from SMDescentYukawaBlocksExact.lean, and chirality with tableChirality b = diag(+1 on Q_L, L_L; -1 on u_R, d_R, e_R(, nu_R)) read off the chirality column of tab:SM-representations; the declared neutral blocks are identified with the neutral rows of the branch (neutralEquiv). Derived consequences: fermionRep and chirality are determined by the table (fermionRep_eq_table, chirality_eq_table), one generation has dimension 15 / 16 (finrank_oneGeneration_minimal / _neutrino), and v is left-handed iff its right-row components vanish (chirality_eq_self_iff). Constructor from data: ofTable builds the record from the (I1), (I3)-(I5) data and the branch, producing the fermion carrier, representation, chirality and the involution/equivariance fields from the table (tableChirality_mul_self, tableChirality_commute). Non-vacuity: trivialGeometryInterface (one site, flat coframe, Gram = id), whose G_SM action is nontrivial (example in the file: the cover element (1, 1, e^{i pi/6}) acts by -1 on e_R). Still disclosed (accepted as minor by the audit): relabeling covariance and the smooth comparison cylinder / reconstruction map of (I1) are not encoded; the Majorana charge-conjugate doubling concerns the bilinear, not the representation rows. Checklist (b): the fermion representation is tied to the table and constructed from it.

S_{g,h} = gravityAction and S_{SM,h} = nu * matterAction of the library interface (so S_h = S_{g,h} + S_{SM,h}: fderiv_action_eq_sum); sectorwise differentiability at z^d is a field. prop:source-bound.title: Scaled source control of physical stationarity
prop:source-bound.note: Proved. The positive source space with Gram G_h is a real inner-product space W (its norm is the G_h norm); the finite action covector a_h is a continuous linear functional a : W ->L[R] R whose operator norm is the dual norm ||a_h||_{G_h^{-1}} (source_bound), equivalently the G_h-norm of its Riesz representative alpha (source_bound_riesz, using innerSL_apply_norm). The test space V is any real normed space (the C^{r_0} norm), v_h : V -> W the source lift, and Phi v = D S_h(z_h^d)[I_h v]. stationarityDefect Phi := iSup over the unit ball of |Phi v| encodes eps_h(K) of eq:stationarity. From ||a||^2 <= R_h, ||v_h(v)|| <= L_h ||v|| and |Phi v - a(v_h v)| <= e_h ||v||, source_bound_pointwise gives |Phi v| <= (L_h sqrt R_h + e_h)||v|| (Cauchy-Schwarz = ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm, sqrt monotonicity, triangle inequality) and source_bound gives eps_h(K) <= L_h sqrt R_h + e_h (ciSup_le over the nonempty unit ball). The 'in particular' clause is source_bound_tendsto: along a regulator sequence, L_h sqrt R_h + e_h -> 0 forces eps_h(K) -> 0 (squeeze_zero with stationarityDefect_nonneg_of_bound). Scoped hypotheses disclosed: the constants L_h, e_h are taken nonnegative (needed only to pass from the ||v||-scaled bound to the unit-ball supremum); the lift v_h need not be linear; the earlier pointer gt_protected_riesz was not needed.

thm:reduced-closure.title: Reduced Einstein--Standard-Model variational closure
thm:reduced-closure.note: Proved. reduced_closure: for a regulator sequence reg (def:regulator) satisfying the reduced compactness certificate (R1)-(R5) on every chart box, first-variation consistency c_h(K)->0 and physical stationarity eps_h(K)->0 for every K (FirstVariationConsistent, PhysicallyStationary; the manuscript's hypothesis L_h sqrt(R_h)+e_h->0 implies eps_h(K)->0 by prop:source-bound, so this is a weakening of the hypothesis), every cutoff subsequence ns has a further subsequence ns o psi, limit fields L and a limiting bank theta0 with: theta0 physical; on every slab chart ReducedConvergence (strong H^1 coframes with terms and limit a.e. in one compact subset of the oriented time-oriented nondegenerate coframe chart, no uniform convergence; A_h->A in L^4 with smLie-valued limit; F_{A_h}->F in L^2 with F=dA+A^A weakly (identity passed to the limit, hasWeakCurvature_of_tendsto); H_h->H, D_{A_h}H_h->D_AH in L^2 with D_AH identified weakly; weak H^1 spinors; bank convergence in the compact physical set) and HiggsH1L4Convergence (H_h->H strongly in H^1 cap L^4 with gradient D_AH - rho_H(A)H, prop:covariant-higgs-endpoint); the complete reconstructed first variation (gravity + Yang-Mills + Higgs + full Dirac-Yukawa) converges in (V_K^{r0})^* (actionVariation_dual_tendsto); the limit is a distributional solution of all Euler equations: gravLimitVariation + smLimitVariation = 0 on every test of every V_K (residual bound eq:reduced-residual-bound: limit_eq_zero_of_defects + homogeneity); eq:reduced-Einstein-limit: einsteinDistribution = kappa * stressDistribution on metric tests, with <(Ein(g)+Lambda g)dV_g,k> := 2 kappa D S_g[k] (first-order/integrated-by-parts representative of app:palatini, gravLimitVariation) and <T^SM dV_g,k> := -2 D_g S_SM[k] (eq:stress-definition, smLimitVariation incl. the spin-connection chain), both evaluated on the metric part (k,0,0,0,0) of the test. Compactness: Rellich (w12_compactness_box) + lem:screen (screen_strong_convergence, with the new links: weak sequential compactness in L^2 and complete continuity of compact operators) for the coframe, curvature and covariant-gradient packets; L^4 precompactness of A; prop:covariant-higgs-endpoint (covariant_higgs_endpoint_box); weak H^1 compactness for spinors; compact bank set; diagonal argument over the slab exhaustion (T/(m+3), T-T/(m+3))x(0,1)^3 with one patched limit (uniqueness of reduced limits a.e. + a.e. invariance). Scoped hypothesis (disclosed): FermionCarrier.YukawaContinuous (the carrier encoding leaves the bank -> Yukawa map abstract; in the manuscript it is a fixed linear function of the bank's Yukawa matrices). Renderings (accepted, disclosed again): M=(0,T)xT^3 lifted to R^4 with spatially Z^3-periodic fields, trivialised bundles, compact charts rendered as chart boxes, H^1(Q)=W^{1,2}(Q) with weak gradients as data, dual norms of V_K^r rendered as the uniform estimate |l_h(v)-l(v)| <= eps ||v||_{C^r} eventually; the conclusions are stated on every slab chart box (t0,t1)x(0,1)^3, 0<t0<t1<T (a fundamental domain of the spatial torus; ReducedConvergence.mono gives every chart box inside a slab; boxes straddling a spatial period differ by a Z^3 translation of periodic fields, not formalised). Non-vacuity: the flat regulator satisfies every hypothesis (flatRegulator_consistent: its continuum first variations vanish, firstVariation_flat; flatRegulator_stationary; example after them). Standard axioms only.

prop:covariant-higgs-endpoint.title: Covariant-gradient compactness closes the Higgs endpoint
prop:covariant-higgs-endpoint.note: Proved on a coordinate box Q = prod_i (a_i, b_i) in a four-dimensional chart (disclosed rendering of the bounded smooth chart K, as for prop:orlicz). Renderings: the Higgs field has m complex components H_h^c, each in H^1(Q) = W^{1,2}(Q) with weak gradient dH_h (the manuscript's smooth reconstructed fields are in particular in H^1(Q); only H^1 is assumed); the connection enters through the matrix entries A_h mu c e = rho_H(A_{h,mu})_{ce} (A_h -> A in L^4 gives entrywise L^4 convergence since rho_H is linear); D_A H = dH + A H (covD). covariant_higgs_endpoint_box: from A_h -> A_0 in L^4(Q), sup_h ||H_h||_{L^2(Q)} < infinity and D_{A_h} H_h -> Y in L^2(Q), a subsequence converges to some H_0 with H_0 in H^1(Q), weak gradient covGrad = Y - A_0 H_0 (i.e. Y = D_{A_0} H_0, covD_covGrad), strongly in H^1(Q) (values and weak gradients in L^2(Q)) and strongly in L^4(Q); covariant_higgs_endpoint_box_precompact: the same for every subsequence (precompactness in H^1(Q)); covariant_higgs_endpoint_box_of_L2: if H_h -> H_0 in L^2(Q) is known (any subsequential L^2 limit), Y = D_{A_0} H_0 and the whole sequence converges in H^1(Q) and L^4(Q); higgs_densities_tendsto: conj(H^c) H^e converge in L^2, the quartic products and conj(D^c_mu) D^e_nu in L^1 (the quartic potential lambda(|H|^2 - v^2)^2 and the Higgs stress are fixed linear combinations of these with constant reference-chart coefficients; for convergent bounded coefficients LpProductContinuity.LpTendsto.coeff applies). Proof as in the manuscript: relative multiplier estimate ||alpha w||_2 <= eps ||w||_4 + C_eps ||w||_2 for fixed alpha in L^4 (truncation, exists_relative_multiplier), critical Sobolev H^1(Q) -> L^4(Q) (eLpNorm_le_box: Mathlib's Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev inequality for C^1_c functions extended to W^{1,2}_c by mollification, eLpNorm_le_sum_grad_of_ball, plus the box extension), absorption giving an eventual uniform H^1 bound (covariant_eventually_bounded), Rellich on the box (rellich_box_family), compact multiplication (tendsto_eLpNorm_mul_of_L4) for A_h H_h -> A_0 H_0 in L^2, passage of weak derivatives to L^2 limits (hasWeakPartial_of_tendsto), and Sobolev on the differences for L^4. lem:products is not used as a hypothesis (the needed Hoelder products are proved here or taken from Analysis/MollifierLpConvergence LpTendsto.bilin). Non-vacuity: example after higgs_densities_tendsto (constant field, zero connection, unit box of R^4). Standard axioms only.

prop:weak-fermion.title: Weak-$H^1$ continuity of the complete fermionic first variation
prop:weak-fermion.note: Proved in the slab-box rendering. diracVariation_dual_tendsto: on the slab chart box Q=(t0,t1)x(0,1)^3 containing the time support of K, if the coframes take values a.e. in one compact subset of the coframe chart and converge strongly in H^1(Q), A_h->A and H_h->H strongly in L^2(Q), Psi_h, Psibar_h converge weakly in H^1(Q) (WeakH1Tendsto) and the Yukawa coefficients converge (linear part in operator norm and constant), then the complete first variation of the Dirac-Yukawa action actionVariation T (diracDensity*volFactor) along variationDirection (metric lift incl. the spin-connection chain omega=P(e)de, gauge, Higgs, spinor variations) converges in the dual norm of V_K^r for every r>=1 (paper: r>=2), rendered as: for all eps>0, eventually |DS_h(v)-DS(v)|<=eps*||v||_{C^r} for all tests. The L^2 hypotheses cover the paper's L^4 form (diracVariation_dual_tendsto_L4) and its weakening (strong L^2 + uniform L^4); no strong convergence of spinor derivatives and no uniform coframe convergence is used. Ingredients: factorization diracDensity*vol = diracPt(redJet) (spinConn_eq_spinConnL), covector split strong/weak, Rellich (tendsto_L2_box_of_weak), Sobolev L^4 (exists_sobolev_L4_box), critical (2,4,4) trilinear products, finite-net weak-strong pairing on the C^1 unit ball (uniform_weak_strong_op). Renderings disclosed: hypotheses on the slab box (a compact neighbourhood of K covering the spatial torus) rather than on K itself; the limit functional diracLimitVariation is the covector formula evaluated on the limit jet (low-regularity D S_D); Yukawa convergence assumed because FermionCarrier.yukawa is an arbitrary function of the bank; the 'no independent fermionic Hilbert-stress defect' sentence is the interpretation of the metric-direction part of the same convergence.

prop:reduced-continuity.note: Proved in the slab-box rendering, all four sectors. actionVariation_dual_tendsto: under ReducedConvergence (def:reduced-topology) on the slab chart box Q=(t0,t1)x(0,1)^3 whose open time interval contains the time support of K (CylRegion.exists_slab_Ioo), and convergence of the carrier's Yukawa map, for every r>=1 (paper r>=2) D S_{theta_h}(z_h) = firstVariation .gravity + firstVariation .standardModel converges to the limit first variation in the dual norm of V_K^r, rendered as: for all eps>0, eventually |DS_h(v)-DS(v)| <= eps*||v||_{C^r} for all tests. prop:sobolev-bosonic.title: A-priori Sobolev bounds imply bosonic strong compactness
prop:sobolev-bosonic.note: Proved on the periodic box T^d (any d; d = 4 for the statement): Rellich-Kondrachov H^s ⋐ H^t for real t < s (rellich_coeff, rellich_L2), the Sobolev embedding H^s ⊂ C^0 for s > d/2 with continuous representative, uniformly convergent Fourier series and ||g||_inf <= C_{s,d} ||f||_{H^s} (exists_continuous_of_memH; lattice sum sum_{Z^d} <n>^{-2s} < inf for s > d/2, summable_sobWeight_rpow_neg), compactness H^s ⋐ C^0 and hence in every L^p (rellich_C0, precompact_of_bounded_memH: for d = 4, s = 2 + sigma, t = 1 this is exactly the e_h step 'strongly in H^1 ∩ L^inf'), and H^s ⊂ C^1 = W^{1,inf} for s > d/2 + 1 (memH_isLineDeriv); the Fourier-side embedding H^s(T^d) ⊂ L^4 for s > d/4 (eLpNorm_four_le_of_memH, ||f||_4 <= Z^{1/4} ||f||_{H^s}, Z = sum <n>^{-4s}: Parseval for P^2 + Cauchy-Schwarz on the convolution fibres + truncation/Fatou; on T^4 this is H^{1+sigma} ⊂ L^4); weak derivatives as Fourier multipliers agreeing with classical ones (weakDeriv, weakDeriv_toLp_eq); L^4 x L^4 -> L^2 product convergence; curvature F = dA + A∧A of matrix potentials and D_A H = dH + rho(A)H converge in L^2 under H^s convergence, s >= 1, s > d/4 (tendsto_curvature_of_H, tendsto_covDeriv_of_H). ASSEMBLY sobolev_bosonic_torus: on T^d with e_h bounded in H^{s_e}, s_e > max(1,d/2), A_h, H_h bounded in H^{s_A}, H^{s_H} > max(1,d/4) (on T^4: 2+sigma, 1+sigma, 1+sigma as in eq:apriori-bosonic) and coefficient banks in a compact set, one subsequence gives e_h -> e in H^1 and uniformly, A_h -> A and H_h -> H in H^1 ∩ L^4, F_{A_h} -> F_A and D_{A_h}H_h -> D_A H in L^2, theta_h -> theta: this is the periodic case of every displayed conclusion eq:apriori-bosonic-convergence. Not proved: (i) the statement is on a bounded smooth region K of the spin cylinder with the fields' Sobolev norms on K; the periodic box is only the special case of periodic fields, and passing from K to a box needs an H^s extension operator for smooth bounded domains (absent); (ii) the clause 'H_h uniformly bounded in L^{4+delta}' (only L^4, with strong L^4 convergence, is proved: the Cauchy-Schwarz fibre argument does not reach p > 4; it needs H^{1+sigma}(4D) ⊂ L^{4+delta}, e.g. discrete Young/Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev on Z^4). Update (local Sobolev pass): on a bounded region rendered as a coordinate box Q the first-order theory is now proved: H^1(Q) = W^{1,2}(Q) via weak derivatives, a bounded extension operator W^{1,2}(Q) -> W^{1,2}_c(R^d) (exists_extension_box, reflection), Rellich H^1(Q) compact in L^2(Q) (rellich_box), the critical embedding H^1(Q) -> L^4(Q) in four dimensions (eLpNorm_le_box; this is the 'strongly in H^1 and hence in L^4' step for A_h and H_h on Q), compact multiplication by L^4 coefficients and L^4 x L^4 -> L^2 products (CovariantGradientCompactness). Still missing for the statement on K: the fractional spaces H^{1+sigma}(K), H^{2+sigma}(K), sigma in (0,1), and their compact embeddings into H^1(K) and C^0(K) on the region itself (needs fractional Sobolev norms on K or higher-order extension operators; the even reflection only preserves H^1), and the clause 'H_h bounded in L^{4+delta}(K)' (H^{1+sigma} -> L^{4+delta} is reached neither by the Cauchy-Schwarz Fourier argument nor by the critical H^1 -> L^4 embedding).

CompactnessCertificate Q z theta, one field per item: (C1) coframes precompact in L^infty(Q), uniformly nondegenerate (|det e_h| >= c > 0 a.e.), bounded in H^1(Q), first-derivative packet with a common compact L^2 screen; (C2) connections precompact in L^4, curvatures bounded in L^2 with a common compact screen; (C3) Higgs bounded in H^1(Q), covariant gradients bounded in L^2 with a common compact screen, and the Orlicz condition: a monotone Phi with Phi(t)/t -> infinity and sup_h int_Q Phi(|H_h|^4) dV_0 < infinity (lower integral of ofReal Phi; equivalent since an increasing Phi is bounded below on [0,infty) and Q is bounded); (C4) SpinorScreenRoute (C4a: Psi, Psibar precompact in L^2, bounded in H^1, first-jet packets with common compact screens) or DiracStabilityRoute (C4b: a compact subslab [t0,t1] x T^3 containing Q, 0 < t0, t1 < T, on which the reconstructed spinors and dual spinors satisfy DiracStabilityHyp = the hypotheses of prop:dirac-stability: first-order systems A^mu d_mu psi + B psi = r (residual defined by the equation, spatially periodic coefficients), Hermitian A^mu (symmetric hyperbolic), A^0 uniformly positive definite, sup_h(||A^mu||_{W^{1,infty}} + ||B||_{L^infty} + ||psi_h||_{L^infty_t H^2_x}) < infinity, coefficients Cauchy in L^infty, initial data psi_h(t0) Cauchy in L^2(T^3), residuals Cauchy in L^2(I x T^3)); (C5) banks in a compact subset of kappa, g_j, lambda_H > 0. Renderings: W^{1,infty} on the slab as 'bounded and Lipschitz' (equivalent on the convex periodic slab); L^infty_t H^2_x as sup over t of sum_{j<=2} ||D^j_y psi(t,.)||_{L^2([0,1)^3)} with classical spatial derivatives (the reconstructions are smooth); 'common compact screen' literally the hypotheses of lem:screen as in def:reduced-certificate (the alternative verification through prop:time-compactness is a sufficient criterion, not a clause). lem:native-discrete-Hodge.title: Exact periodic discrete Hodge identity
lem:native-discrete-Hodge.note: periodicHodge_identity: on any finite additive commutative group X (the periodic grid, e.g. (ZMod N)^4) with lattice steps e_mu, directions a finite linearly ordered type (Fin 4), values in a real inner product space (Lie algebra with invariant inner product), and every mesh h, sum_{mu,nu} ||D^+_mu A_nu||^2_{2,h} = ||d_h^+ A||^2_{2,h} + ||delta_h A||^2_{2,h}, with ||u||^2_{2,h} = h^{dim} sum_x |u(x)|^2, D^+ forward difference, delta_h A = -sum_mu D^-_mu A_mu (eq:native-discrete-divergence), ||d^+A||^2 = sum_{mu<nu} ||D^+_mu A_nu - D^+_nu A_mu||^2. Proof in position space (translation invariance of periodic sums) rather than Fourier. periodicHodge_H1_bound: for h >= 0, ||A||_{1,h} <= 1*(||d^+A|| + ||delta A|| + ||A||_{2,h}) with ||A||^2_{1,h} = sum_nu ||A_nu||^2 + sum_{mu,nu} ||D^+_mu A_nu||^2 (C = 1, uniform in h).

thm:native-discrete-Coulomb.title: Critical discrete Coulomb compactness
thm:native-discrete-Coulomb.note: Proved (NativeCoulomb.native_discrete_Coulomb), unit-torus rendering (grid (Z/N)^4, mesh h = 1/N, side 1; the paper's odd grids of side 2pi are the dilation, every N allowed). Disclosed renderings: connections take values in a finite-dimensional complete normed complex algebra A with ||1|| = 1 (e.g. M_n(C) with the operator norm, containing the compact gauge algebras; complex scalars only enter the Cauchy estimate of the plaquette remainder); the Lie-algebra norms are read in a real inner product space E through T : A ->L[R] E with ||X|| <= c||T X|| (Frobenius identification for u(n)); the smallness ||A_h||_{4,h} <= eps* is imposed componentwise (||T A_{h,mu}||_{4,h} <= eps* for every mu, weaker than the summed norm); eps* = 1/(69120(||T||+1)(c+1)^2) is explicit. Statement: there is eps* > 0 such that for every sequence of grids N_k -> oo and nodal connections with delta_h T A_k = 0 (codiffT = -sum_mu D^-_mu, the paper's eq:native-discrete-divergence), ||T A_{k,mu}||_{4,h} <= eps* and R_h^0 F_h(A_k) -> F strongly in L^2 (F_h = curvLog, the literal logarithmic plaquette), after extraction: R_h^0 A_k -> A strongly in L^4; R_h^0 D+_mu A_{k,nu} -> G_{mu nu} strongly in L^2 with G_{mu nu} = d_mu A_nu (Fourier side, every frequency); for every complex coordinate l of A, l A_nu in H^1 and the trigonometric reconstructions I_h^trig(l A_k) -> l A in H^1; F = F_A pointwise a.e. (F_{mu nu} = d_mu A_nu - d_nu A_mu + [A_mu, A_nu]); delta A = 0 (sum_mu d_mu A_mu = 0 a.e.). Proof as in the manuscript, all clauses formalized: (i) the Lipschitz half of eq:native-YM-envelope, ||N_h(A) - N_h(B)|| <= 5(|W(A)| + |W(B)|)|W(A-B)| pointwise and its L^2_h form (norm_nonlin_sub_le, gridNorm_nonlin_sub_le; from the new Cauchy-estimate Lipschitz bound for the cubic BCH remainder, PlaquetteLogDerivative.norm_bchRem_sub_le); (ii) the absorption inequality eq:native-Coulomb-explicit-absorption with explicit constants (coulomb_absorption: exact Hodge identity + uniform grid Sobolev + envelope), which with B = 0 is the a priori H^1 bound; (iii) discrete Rellich componentwise, L^1 convergence of the nonlinear term and the exact Fourier multipliers of the grid differences identify F = dA + A^A and delta A = 0 on the Fourier side; (iv) comparison fields = Fourier truncations P_R A of the limit (divergence free; P_R A -> A in L^2 and, by the new critical embedding H^1(T^4) c L^4 obtained from the discrete Sobolev inequality by sampling, tendsto_eLpNorm_four_trunc, in L^4; F_{P_R A} -> F), sampled on the grids with fixed-smooth-field consistency; absorption gives limsup_h ||D+A_h - dP_R A||_{L^2} <= c delta_R -> 0, hence the forward differences are Cauchy in L^2 (exists_tendsto_differences); (v) lem:native-reconstruction-identification gives the L^4 and trigonometric H^1 statements and prop:native-YM-identification (first assertion, native_YM_curvature_identification) gives F = F_A pointwise. The convention bridge between CoulombAprioriEstimate/PeriodicForwardDifferenceHodgeIdentityExact (general mesh h, side L = n h, E-valued) and the unit-torus files is NativeCoulombAbsorption (h = 1/N, L = 1, periodicHodgeNormSq = gridNorm^2, gridFwd = DpV, T-read values); the a priori estimate is reproved there in unit-torus notation (coulomb_apriori'). Non-vacuity: example at the end of NativeCoulombCompactness (zero connections in A = C). Standard axioms only.

lem:native-log-gauge-differential.title: Exact logarithmic site-gauge differential
lem:native-log-gauge-differential.note: Both identities proved on the periodic grid (Z/n)^iota (any finite iota, any mesh h != 0), with the gauge group in the units of an arbitrary complete normed real algebra A (nontrivial; for SU(3)xSU(2): pairs of complex matrices) and Lie-algebra fields A_mu(x), xi_x in A, ad_A u = Au - uA. New generic infrastructure (Algebra/MatrixExpDerivative.lean, absent from Mathlib, which differentiates exp only along commuting directions): Duhamel e^A - e^B = int_0^1 e^{sA}(A-B)e^{(1-s)B} ds; D exp(X)[Y] = int_0^1 e^{sX} Y e^{(1-s)X} ds; e^{s ad_X}Y = e^{sX}Y e^{-sX}; int_0^1 e^{sZ} ds = J(Z) = sum Z^k/(k+1)! (OperatorHalfCoth.dexpJ); hence the dexp formula D exp(X)[Y] = (J(ad_X)Y) e^X (fderiv_exp_eq, the paper's left-trivialized U'U^{-1} = h J(Z) A'); strict differentiability with invertible derivative when J(ad_X) is a unit (e.g. ||X|| <= 1/8); every local left inverse Log of exp near X (the logarithm chart) is strictly differentiable at e^X with derivative W -> J(ad_X)^{-1}(W e^{-X}) (hasStrictFDerivAt_log_of_eventually); d/dt Log(e^{t xi} e^X e^{-t eta})|_0 = J(ad_X)^{-1}(xi - e^{ad_X} eta). Gauge application (GaugeTheory/LogarithmicSiteGaugeDifferential.lean): gaugeCurve = A^{q(t)}_mu(x) = h^{-1} Log(e^{t xi_x} e^{hA_mu(x)} e^{-t xi_{x+e_mu}}). gauge_differential (eq:native-gauge-differential): if Log(e^Y) = Y near every h A_mu(x) (any fixed chart containing the scaled links; conjugation invariance not needed) and every J(h ad_{A_mu(x)}) is invertible, then A^{q(0)} = A and d/dt A^{q(t)}_mu(x)|_0 = -K(h ad_{A_mu}) D^+_mu xi(x) - [A_mu(x), m_mu xi(x)], K(Z) = (Z/2)coth(Z/2) = 1/2 J(Z)^{-1}(I + e^Z) (OperatorHalfCoth.halfCoth), via J^{-1}(I - e^Z) = -Z exactly as in the paper. gauge_energy_differential (eq:native-gauge-energy-differential): for any symmetric continuous bilinear form <.,.> on A with <A_mu(x), [A_mu(x), u]> = 0 (implied by ad-invariance + symmetry of the paper's positive invariant metric, e.g. Re tr(X^*Y) with A anti-Hermitian), d/dt 1/2 ||A^{q(t)}||^2_{2,h}|_0 = -<delta_h A, xi>_{2,h}, ||a||^2_{2,h} = h^d sum_{mu,x} <a_mu(x),a_mu(x)>, delta_h A = -sum_mu D^-_mu A_mu; uses <A, K(h ad_A) v> = <A, v> (pairing_halfCoth, the paper's K^*A = A) and summation by parts. Non-vacuity: gauge_hypotheses_nonvacuous (any field with ||h A_mu(x)|| <= 1/8, e.g. A = 0, has invertible J's and a local logarithm chart; exists_log_chart). All cited declarations: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

lem:native-FP-inverse.title: Uniform transverse inverse
lem:native-FP-inverse.note: Proved on the periodic grid (Z/n)^iota with card iota = 4 (any n >= 1, mesh h > 0, side L = n h). Encoding: the Lie algebra is a finite-dimensional nontrivial real inner product space E with an arbitrary continuous bilinear bracket br (invariance of the metric and the Jacobi identity are not needed, so this is more general than the paper); K(Z) = (Z/2)coth(Z/2) is encoded through the paper identity K(Z) = 1/2 J(Z)^{-1}(I + e^Z) with J(Z) = sum_k Z^k/(k+1)! = int_0^1 e^{tZ} dt (eq:native-JK; OperatorHalfCoth.halfCoth, an analytic function, Z J(Z) = e^Z - 1 (mul_dexpJ), scalar check halfCoth z (e^z - 1) = (z/2)(e^z + 1) (halfCoth_real_mul), K(0) = I, ||K(Z) - I|| <= 12||Z||^2 on ||Z|| <= 1/4 (norm_halfCoth_sub_one_le)); M_A xi = delta_h(K(h ad_{A_mu}) D^+_mu xi + [A_mu, m_mu xi]) with delta_h = -sum D^-_mu (FaddeevPopov.fpOp, eq:native-FP). With r_FP = 1/(64(||br||+1)), independent of n and h, and the hypothesis ||A_mu||_{4,h} < r_FP for every direction mu (implied by the paper hypothesis ||A||_{4,h} < r_FP for the pointwise norm): fp_coercive: <M_A xi, xi>_{2,h} >= 1/2 ||D^+ xi||^2_{2,h} on the mean-zero space Z_h (eq:native-FP-coercivity; proof as in the paper: h||A||_inf <= ||A||_{4,h}, ||K - I|| <= C h^2|A|^2, weighted Hoelder L^4 x L^4 x L^2, ||m xi||_4 <= ||xi||_4, mean-zero Sobolev grid_sobolev_poincare_meanZero_l2); fp_bijective: M_A : Z_h -> Z_h bijective (exists unique mean-zero solution); fp_dual_inverse_sSup: ||D^+ M_A^{-1} f||_{2,h} <= 2 ||f||_{H^{-1}_h} with the dual norm defined as the sSup over mean-zero zeta with ||D^+ zeta||_{2,h} = 1 (dualNorm, abs_gridInner_le_dualNorm) (eq:native-FP-dual-inverse); fp_divergence_inverse: ||M_A^{-1} delta_h R||_{2,h} + ||M_A^{-1} delta_h R||_{4,h} + ||D^+ M_A^{-1} delta_h R||_{2,h} <= (2 + 2 sqrt2 L + 4(3 + 2 sqrt2)) ||R||_{2,h} (eq:native-FP-divergence-inverse; constant independent of n for the fixed box L = 2 pi); fp_inverse_contDiffOn: on {A : ||A_mu||_{4,h} < r_FP} the extension N_A xi = M_A(xi - mean xi) + mean xi is invertible, A -> N_A^{-1} is C^k for every k (smooth and analytic orders), and N_A^{-1} f is the mean-zero solution of M_A xi = f for mean-zero f (smooth dependence of the inverse). Non-vacuity: example with A = 0 (M_0 = delta_h D^+). No self-adjointness of M_A is used. All cited declarations use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

thm:finite-Coulomb-normalization.title: Finite critical Coulomb normalization
thm:finite-Coulomb-normalization.note: Proved for the paper's exact gauge group G_SM = S(U(3)xU(2)) (eq:gauge-group): StandardModelCoulomb.finite_coulomb_normalization_SM. Setting: 4D periodic grid (ZMod n)^iota, card iota = 4, mesh h, box side L = n h GENERAL (the paper fixes L = 2pi; constants depend only on L and the group/metric, never on n or h); A_SM = M3(C) x M2(C) with operator norms, invariant Frobenius metric Re tr(X3^*Y3) + Re tr(X2^*Y2) (toESM). Statement: for every eps_* > 0 there are eps_c, C_c > 0 such that every g_SM-valued seed B (skew-Hermitian blocks, tr B3 + tr B2 = 0) with ||B||_{4,h} + ||F_h(B)||_{2,h} <= eps_c admits a site gauge q with q_x in S(U(3)xU(2)) (unitary, det q3 * det q2 = 1) such that A = h^-1 Log(q_x e^{hB} q_{x+mu}^*) (linkA h B 1 q; FiniteCoulomb.linkA_at_one) is g_SM-valued (skew, tr A3 + tr A2 = 0), delta_h A = 0, ||A||_{1,h} + ||A||_{4,h} <= C_c(||B||_{2,h} + ||F_h(B)||_{2,h} + ||B||_{4,h}^2) and ||A||_{4,h} <= eps_*. NORM CONVENTION (disclosed): ||A||_{4,h} := sum_mu ||A_mu||_{4,h} (equivalent within fixed factors to the l4 combination of the components), ||A||_{2,h}^2 = sum_mu ||A_mu||_{2,h}^2, ||A||_{1,h} as in lem:native-reconstruction-identification, ||F||_{2,h} over mu<nu. Proof: general theorem FiniteCoulomb.finite_coulomb_normalization (unitary group of any finite-dim C*-algebra with invariant metric; the paper's homotopy ODE q' = xi q, xi = M_{A_s}^-1 delta_h R_s, Coulomb preservation, L^2 energy bound, curvature covariance + exact split, a priori a <= C_0 b + C_1 a^2, first exit, global existence via ODEContinuation.exists_solution_of_apriori); trace constraint along the path (CoulombTrace.trace_linkA_of_solution with tau = Re/Im(tr3 + tr2)) gives tr A3 + tr A2 = 0; then det(e^{hA}) = e^{tau(hA)} = 1 (MatrixDetExp.det_exp_eq_complex_exp_trace) on every link gives chi(q_x) chi(q_{x+mu})^* = 1 for chi = det3*det2, so chi(q) is a constant unit d, and the constant central phase c (c^5 = d^-1) gives the gauge c q in S(U(3)xU(2)) with the same links (the determinant clause is obtained by this post-hoc central correction rather than a Liouville ODE along the path; same conclusion). Also: U(N) (FrobeniusCoulomb), SU(N) (SpecialUnitaryCoulomb), general trace-constrained version (CoulombTrace); non-vacuity: FrobeniusCoulomb.exists_coulomb_zero_seed. Log = analytic series branch near 1 (conjugation-invariant chart).

FiniteStandardModelActionGaugeCovarianceExact.higgsEdgeDifference_gauge); Dirac via V_mu(g.y) = rho_S(g_x) V_mu rho_S(g_{x+mu})^-1 and commutation with sigma, gamma, Yukawa covariance; gravity sector carries no internal link. lem:determinant-screen-flux.title: Determinant compactness, admissibility, and flux
lem:determinant-screen-flux.note: All clauses proved (determinant_screen_flux) on the paper's periodic box of side L > 0 (2 pi in the paper), four-dimensional grids (Z/n_k)^4 with n_k -> infinity, h_k = L/n_k (oddness not needed). Hypotheses (structure CurvatureScreen, exactly the lemma's): G_SM links U_k; for every oriented pair mu<nu an arbitrary logarithm L_k(x,mu,nu) of the full plaquette (exp in both factors = P_{U,mu nu}(x); no chart and no bound on link logarithms assumed); literal full curvature packet F_k = (h^-2 L_k)_{mu<nu} bounded in L^2_h; full-box adjoint Wilson screen lim_{rho->0} limsup_k Omega_h(F;rho) = 0 used for positive displacements m h <= rho (implied by the paper's |m| h <= rho). Norm rendering: operator (unitarily invariant) norm on each matrix factor, max norm on pairs and on the six-component packet; equivalent to the invariant Euclidean metric up to a dimensional constant (boundedness/vanishing moduli unchanged); Ad acts by linear isometries (adPair, adPacket). Conclusions: (1) eventually f_h = l_c(F_h) exactly (eventually_detPacket; via eventual uniform smallness of h^2 F_h = L_h (eventually_small: scalar-magnitude uniform integrability from the proved thm:native-Wilson-compactness, exists_tail_le and the cell mass h^4) and DeterminantFlux.ellC_eq_arg_smChi); (2) eventually ||T_{mu,m} f - f||_{2,h} <= 2 ||W_{mu,m} F - F||_{2,h} for all mu, m >= 0 (Ad-invariance of l_c, ellC_openLink; |l_c| <= 2||.||), hence omega_h(f;rho) <= 2 Omega_h(F;rho) (negative ordinary shifts have the same norms by translation invariance); (3) max_{x,mu,nu} |phi_{mu nu,h}(x)| -> 0 (all ordered pairs, via abPhase_swap/abPhase_self); (4) R_h^0 f_h precompact in L^2 (TotallyBounded, unit-torus rendering of native_discrete_KR as for lem:native-discrete-KR); (5) eventually d_h f_h = 0 exactly (all cube sums vanish); (6) every coordinate-plane flux is 2 pi m, m integer (all k); eventually base-point independent, mean curvature L^-4 h^4 sum f = 2 pi m / L^2 and 2 pi |m| <= ||f_{mu nu}||_{2,h} (from determinant_screen_flux_exact / mean_curvature_eq_flux / two_pi_abs_flux_le); (7) the integer vectors (m_{mu nu,h})_{mu<nu} are bounded (2 pi |m| <= ||f|| <= 2||F||) and constant along a strictly increasing subsequence (pigeonhole, Finite.exists_infinite_fiber). Non-vacuity: curvatureScreen_trivial (trivial links, zero logarithms). Also closes prop:native-determinant-split (extra key, see there). All cited new declarations: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

prop:periodic-determinant-normalization.title: Zero-flux Abelian normalization with unrestricted flat holonomy
prop:periodic-determinant-normalization.note: Clause-level status: ALL CLAUSES PROVED. lem:native-plaquette.note: Proved in a real Banach algebra 𝔄 with ‖1‖ = 1 (NormOneClass; scoped hypothesis, as in the previous partial), for X, Y, a, b in 𝔄. Bundled statement exists_joint_analytic_extension: there is Φ : ℝ × 𝔄⁴ → 𝔄 (jointLogPlaquette) with (i) Φ analytic at every (0, X, Y, a, b), (ii) Φ(0; X,Y,a,b) = a - b + [X,Y], (iii) h² Φ(h) = log(e^{hX} e^{h(Y+ha)} e^{-h(X+hb)} e^{-hY}) for all h ≠ 0 with the series logarithm log(1+z) = z Σ (-1)^n z^n/(n+1), and (iv) for every order k and every compact set K of parameters there are h₀ > 0 and C with ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ k Φ (h, q)‖ ≤ C for |h| ≤ h₀ and q ∈ K, i.e. all fixed-order derivatives in h and in the parameters are uniformly bounded on compact argument sets for small h (second sentence of the lemma). Method for (i)/(iv): exp u = 1 + u + u² E(u) with E entire (exp_eq_expRemainder), giving the explicit removable quotient P(h) - 1 = h² Q(h; X,Y,a,b) with Q a polynomial in h, X, Y, a, b and the E(h v_i) (product_sub_one_eq), equal to the dslope quotient of the previous partial for every h (quotient_eq_quotientPoly); Φ = Q · L(h² Q) is then jointly analytic on the open set ‖h² Q‖ < 1 ⊇ {0} × 𝔄⁴, and the bound (iv) follows by continuity of iteratedFDeriv on a compact tube [-h₀, h₀] × K (generalized tube lemma). prop:native-rounding.title: A sufficient nodal-accuracy condition
prop:native-rounding.note: Proved on the periodic grid (Fin 4 -> ZMod n) with the normalized four-dimensional DFT u^(l) = n^{-4} sum_x e(-l.x) u(x) defined from the product of Mathlib's standard characters ZMod.stdAddChar: character orthogonality sum_l e(l.x) = n^4 [x = 0] (sum_char4) and Parseval sum_l ||u^(l)||^2 = n^{-4} sum_x ||u(x)||^2 (sum_norm_dft4_sq). Modes are measured by centred representatives ZMod.valMinAbs (|l|_1 = sum_mu |l_mu|, tail set |l|_inf > K), so Lambda_h is the mode lattice and tau_{h,j}(K) of eq:native-tail is the definition tau. eq:native-rounding-tail: if u = u^b + e with u^b Fourier-supported in |l|_inf <= K and max_x ||e(x)|| <= eps, then with h = 2 pi / n and hK <= 1, tau_{h,j}(K) <= (1 + 4 pi)^j 4 pi^2 eps h^{-2} (hK)^{-j} (tau_le_of_bandLimited_add; explicit C_j). eq:native-rounding-tolerance: eps <= c h^{m+3} K^{m+2} gives tau_{h,m} <= C_m c hK^2 (tau_le_of_tolerance) and, with m = k + 2, tau_{h,2} <= C_2 c (h^k K^{k+1}) hK, so tau_{h,2} = O(hK) as soon as h^k K^{k+1} is bounded, which holds on the rate families K ~ h^{-beta}, beta < 1/(k+4), of cor:native-rate (tau_two_le_of_tolerance, with the family entering through the explicit hypothesis h^k K^{k+1} <= A). Scoped hypotheses (disclosed): hK <= 1 (the paper's standing hK <= c_res), K real positive, the record valued in a complex inner-product space E (real-valued records embed in C^d), n is any nonzero integer (oddness is not needed), and the 'affine field-chart constraints' clause plays no role in the inequality.

prop:native-reader.title: Exact native-energy to physical-tail certificate
prop:native-reader.note: Finite-dimensional linear algebra, fully proved; the revised statement matches the Lean even more closely than the old one. Source space H = finite-dimensional real inner-product space, native energy Q symmetric with <xi,Q xi> >= 0, coefficient map T : H -> (modes -> F) linear, positive weights w, tail tau_w(v) = sum_l w_l ||v_l|| (the l^1(w) norm). eq:source-reader-linear / eq:source-reader-kernel: exists_readerConstant_iff_kernel states that a finite c with ||T xi||_{l^1(w)} <= c <xi,Q xi>^{1/2} for ALL xi in H (IsReaderConstant, quantified over the entire source space, so not inferred from a finite list of legal states) exists iff T(ker Q) = 0 (KernelCondition). eq:source-reader-constant: readerConstant := ||T Q^{dagger/2}||_{2->l^1(w)} = sup_{||y||<=1} tau_w(T Q^{dagger/2} y), with Q^{dagger/2} = SpectralDiag.pinvSqrt built from Mathlib's finite spectral theorem (lambda_i^{-1/2} on the nonzero spectrum, 0 on the kernel); symmetric, positive, and its square satisfies the Penrose identities Q Q^dagger Q = Q and Q^dagger Q Q^dagger = Q^dagger (Q_pinvSq_Q, pinvSq_Q_pinvSq), so it is the positive square root of the Moore-Penrose inverse; readerConstant_isLeast: under the kernel condition this constant is admissible and is the least nonnegative admissible constant. eq:source-reader-tail ("in particular"): affine_reader_tail derives tau_w(u^soft + T xi) <= tau_w(u^soft) + c <xi,Q xi>^{1/2} for the affine reader u = u^soft + R xi by the triangle inequality. prop:constraint-extension.title: Residual-preserving extension of a constrained identity
prop:constraint-extension.note: Proved. Chart (s,c) ∈ E_s × E_c (real normed spaces), J : E_s × E_c → F C¹ into a complete normed space F (matrix-valued maps: F = matrices with any norm), D_cJ(s,c) = fderiv of c' ↦ J(s,c'). constraintExtension_ftc: eq:constraint-extension J(s,c) = J(s,0) + ∫₀¹ D_cJ(s,tc)[c] dt (FTC along the normal segment). constraintTracking: for ċ = A(t)c + r(t) on [0,T] with ∫₀ᵀ‖A‖ ≤ M and ‖c(0)‖ + ∫₀ᵀ‖r‖ ≤ C a^p, ‖c(t)‖ ≤ C e^M a^p for all t ∈ [0,T] (eq:constraint-tracking), from the Gronwall bound constraintTracking_le ‖c(t)‖ ≤ e^M(‖c(0)‖ + ∫₀ᵀ‖r‖), proved by an ε-perturbed comparison function e^{∫₀ᵗ‖A‖}(‖c(0)‖ + ε + ∫₀ᵗ‖r‖ + εt) and Mathlib's image_norm_le_of_norm_deriv_right_lt_deriv_boundary. constraintExtension_matrix_estimate: ‖D_cJ‖ ≤ L uniformly gives ‖J(s(t),c(t)) − J(s(t),0)‖ ≤ L·C e^M a^p on [0,T] (the O(a^p) matrix estimate). Scoped hypotheses disclosed: the tracking equation holds classically (c continuous on [0,T] with right derivative A(t)c(t) + r(t) on [0,T), A and r continuous on [0,T]) rather than in the Carathéodory/L¹ sense.
